title: Simple Rules, Visualized (Teaching Simplified Series, August 2022)
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Continuing his August 2022 Teaching Simplified series, Dave devotes this entry to time-management boundaries, introducing "the inner work of the teacher" as a recurring through-line. He shares his own weekday and Saturday work-hour rules, explains why visualizing those boundaries (not just deciding on them) makes them stick, and urges teachers to communicate their rules to an accountability partner. The piece is grounded in an anecdote from a school visit in Linden, CA, that sparked his thinking on why inner, unglamorous habits matter as much as classroom technique.
points: Introduces "the inner work of the teacher" as a skill/muscle worth deliberately developing, distinct from external/technical teaching skills.
Recommends setting explicit, hard-stop working-hour rules (a defined weekday end time, a capped Saturday morning) rather than a vague intention to "work less."
Argues that visualizing the rules — seeing the boundary, not just deciding on it mentally — is what makes the limits stick.
Advises sharing your work-hour rules with an accountability partner and expecting, even welcoming, the friction the rules will cause.
quotes: And here, colleague, is through line number one: the inner work of the teacher. It's a thing. It's a skill. It's a muscle. Grow it, and delight. Neglect it, and pine.
Set simple rules that place boundaries around your working hours this coming school year. Here are mine.
Monday through Friday: I can work from whenever I wake up until I need to be home from work, which is 5:00 or 5:30 pm depending on the night's agenda. And do no work at home!
As I discuss in the video — these work for me and my family. They're not better or worse than yours. Whatever your constraints are, my encouragement to you is to accept and embrace them.
Communicate these rules with someone who will hold you accountable. Be prepared for these rules to cause you problems, and please — let these problems help you!
